brief.label: Pull-force + mechanical test methods
items: ASTM F2213 pull-force test apparatus — perpendicular pull-off force on standard steel substrate at 20 °C ambient.
Proud Tek PT-MAG-2024 test procedure — pull-force on flat mild-steel (AISI 1018) 6 mm thick, Ra 0.8 μm finish, 20 °C ± 2 °C, 50 % RH.
Shear-force = 20-25 % of perpendicular pull-force for NdFeB on smooth steel.
Curvature derating — pull-force on cylindrical surface reduced by factor (r_magnet / r_surface)^0.5 per empirical fit; > 50 mm surface radius recommended.
Air-gap sensitivity — pull-force decays with (distance / thickness)^3 — paint / rust / contamination reduce effective pull-force significantly.

sections.title: Why adhesive + weld-mount + bolt-on RFID tags fail for repositionable-asset workflows
bullets: Adhesive RFID tags on leased / rented equipment violate commercial lease + rental terms (ARA Rental Agreement Section 7 standard clause) and leave residue that triggers $150-400 per-tag cleaning / surface-restoration charges at return. Adhesive also fails on oil-contaminated mining, construction, and heavy-industrial surfaces within 30 days.

Returnable-transport-item (RTI) pools cycle steel stillages, roll-cages, IBCs, and tote-bins between multiple facilities and owners. RTI pool-operator GS1 GRAI-96 reassignment at the hand-off point requires physically-detachable tags. Welded or bolted tags cannot be swapped between pool members (CHEP / LOSCAM / Euro Pool System / IFCO / IPP).

Tool-crib tracking in machine shops, mold-making, aerospace MRO, and die cells rotates $50,000-500,000 in tooling between machines and departments weekly. Permanent adhesive / weld tags cannot be economically rewritten each reassignment, and manual handwritten logs create the 5-15 % annual tool-loss rate reported by SME 2024 Tool Management Benchmarking Survey.

Warehouse racking + shelving + slot-labelling reconfigurations in dynamic 3PL / e-commerce fulfillment centres happen quarterly; fixed tags on rack positions become invalid at each reconfig, but repositionable magnet-mount tags follow the new rack layout in minutes without re-printing labels or re-encoding RFID substrates.

Construction equipment + scaffolding + shoring + formwork moves between job sites every 2-8 weeks. Adhesive tags fail on vibration + UV + dust + moisture within days, and bolt-on tags require shop time + drilling equipment that on-site crews cannot justify for temporary asset pools.

MRI-suite ferromagnetic-asset identification under ASTM F2503 + The Joint Commission EC.02.06.05 requires tags that can be inventoried outside Zone IV but reliably removed before entering Zone III/IV — permanent tags cannot be removed; weld-mount tags on gurneys / IV-poles cannot clear MR-Safe screening.

sections.title: 18 kg of grip, zero drilled holes
sections.intro: The stack is the trick: UV-stabilised housing, on-metal PCB antenna, a 0.3-1.0 mm Ni-Zn ferrite sheet, then the permanent-magnet base. The ferrite keeps the magnet from swallowing the signal — so a tag that snaps onto any ferromagnetic steel surface still reads like a proper on-metal tag.

bullets: Four magnet chemistries: NdFeB N42 / N52 workhorses (3 kg and 18 kg pull), Sm2Co17 for 350 °C continuous service, ferrite Y30 for corrosion-free economy, AlNiCo 5 at -0.02 %/K for precision estates.
Pull-force rated per the PT-MAG-2024 procedure on 6 mm AISI 1018 steel at Ra 0.8 — with curvature and air-gap derating documented, because paint and rust are real.
Monza R6-P, UCODE 9, EM4325 and Higgs-9 class UHF ICs; optional EM4325-based temperature sensing for cold-chain RTIs and bearing checks.

Housings in ABS / PC-ABS / PA66-GF30, IP67-IP69K per IEC 60529, shock 30 g 11 ms and vibration per IEC 60068-2 — service -40 °C to +80 °C standard, +125 °C high-temp SmCo SKU, up to +230 °C with AH-grade NdFeB.

sections.title: The tag moves with the fleet
sections.intro: Adhesive commits to one surface for one life; welding commits to hot-work permits on somebody else's asset. A magnet commits to nothing: snap on, read at 2-5 m, pry off clean, snap onto the next asset — and re-assign the GRAI-96 / GIAI-96 in the EPCIS record.

bullets: Built for churn: RTI pools (stillages, roll-cages, IBCs), tool cribs and mold / jig / gauge estates, rental and construction plant under OSHA 1910.178 workflows with ISO 19014 + ISO 17757 machinery-safety alignment.
Ships as ordinary cargo when packaging keeps the external field at or under 0.00525 gauss at 4.6 m per IATA DGR 2.14 / 49 CFR 173.21(d).
MR suites are the exception: ASTM F2503 classification applies, and magnet-mount tags stay outside the magnet room.

sections.title: IATA DGR + 49 CFR 173.21 + ICAO magnetized-material transport classification
bullets: IATA DGR Section II 2.14 — magnetized material is defined as any package with magnetic field strength exceeding 0.00525 gauss (0.525 µT) at 4.6 m (15 ft) from any point on the outer package surface; below threshold = not dangerous goods + shipping unrestricted.
49 CFR 173.21(d) US DOT air-carriage threshold — ≤ 0.002 gauss at 2.1 m (7 ft) for air shipments (more restrictive than surface).
ICAO Technical Instructions Doc 9284 Part 2;9.7 — aircraft master compass deflection limit; magnetized material above threshold shipped as UN 2807 Class 9.

Proud Tek packaging-engineering optimization — magnetic field attenuated via MU-metal or silicon-steel shielding laminate + arrangement-geometry so that default carton + pallet configuration passes the 0.00525 / 0.002 gauss thresholds for N42 / N40 / AlNiCo / Ferrite / SmCo SKUs.
N52 heavy-duty 50 × 10 mm SKU ships in single-unit box under threshold; full-pallet configuration exceeds threshold and ships as UN 2807 Class 9 or requires MU-metal shielded tote.
IMDG Code Class 9 sea + ADR Class 9 European road + RID Class 9 rail adopted thresholds align with IATA DGR.

sections.title: ASTM F2503 MR-Conditional / MR-Unsafe classification for medical-suite asset tagging
bullets: ASTM F2503-20 three-tier labelling — MR Safe (no known hazard), MR Conditional (safe under specified MR conditions), MR Unsafe (known hazard). Permanent-magnet RFID tags are inherently MR Unsafe on NdFeB + SmCo + AlNiCo variants due to ferromagnetic attraction in static B₀ field.
ASTM F2052 displacement-force test — measurement at 1.5 T and 3.0 T scanner bore entrance; magnet tag displacement force typically 50-500 × gravitational force depending on size + grade.
ASTM F2213 torque test — magnetic moment m × B_0 creates torque up to 100 N·cm for 50 × 10 mm N52 in 3.0 T field; free-space rotation of unclamped tag.
ASTM F2119 + F2182 imaging artifact + RF-induced heating tests not directly applicable to passive RFID tag but important for device context.

The Joint Commission EC.02.06.05 + ACR Guidance Document on MR Safe Practices — Zone I / II / III / IV access control, ferromagnetic detection system (FMDS) at Zone III/IV boundary, screening checklist — RFID tag-in must be removed before Zone III entry.

Ferrite Y30 SKU is MR-Conditional at 1.5 T / 3.0 T per ASTM F2503 — its lower magnetization and ceramic non-ferromagnetic character produces attraction force below scanner-manufacturer thresholds (typically 10 × gravity). Recommended for MRI-suite-proximity tool crib.

faq.question: Which permanent-magnet grade should I choose for my application?
faq.answer: Use NdFeB N42 low-profile for light-duty tool-crib + warehouse at ambient < 80 °C. Use NdFeB N52 heavy-duty for heavy-industrial / marine / mining RTI at ambient < 80 °C where maximum 18 kg pull-force matters. Use SmCo Sm₂Co₁₇ for steam / forge / paint-line service up to 350 °C. Use hard-ferrite Y30 for economy bulk deployments and MR-Conditional medical proximity. Use AlNiCo 5 for precision-measurement applications requiring −0.02 %/K thermal stability. Use NdFeB N40 countersunk 316L sanitary for pharma / dairy / beverage / bioprocess CIP-washdown RTI.

faq.question: What is the magnetized-material transport classification for these SKUs?
faq.answer: Proud Tek pre-packages each SKU so that the default single-unit carton passes IATA DGR Section II 2.14 + 49 CFR 173.21(d) + ICAO TI 2;9.7 magnetized-material thresholds (≤ 0.00525 gauss at 4.6 m, ≤ 0.002 gauss at 2.1 m for air). Single-unit shipments of all six SKUs are unrestricted. Full-pallet configurations of the N52 heavy-duty SKU exceed threshold and ship as UN 2807 Class 9 dangerous goods or require MU-metal shielded tote — we provide the mu-metal carton at no additional charge for bulk orders.

faq.question: Is the magnet-mount tag safe to use near MRI scanners?
faq.answer: Only the Ferrite Y30 SKU is MR-Conditional at 1.5 T and 3.0 T per ASTM F2503-20. NdFeB + SmCo + AlNiCo SKUs are MR Unsafe because the displacement force per ASTM F2052 and torque per ASTM F2213 exceed scanner-manufacturer limits inside Zone III/IV. For MRI-suite tool-crib and RTI workflows we recommend the Ferrite Y30 SKU and screening via ferromagnetic detection system (FMDS) at the Zone III/IV boundary per ACR Guidance Document on MR Safe Practices.

faq.question: How many times can the tag be repositioned without losing magnetic strength?
faq.answer: NdFeB, SmCo, and AlNiCo permanent-magnet grades maintain > 99 % of initial magnetization after thousands of install / remove cycles at ambient temperature. Demagnetization only occurs under (a) exceeding the grade's max operating temperature, (b) exposure to an external field stronger than Hcj (intrinsic coercivity — approximately 12-35 kOe), or (c) severe mechanical impact sufficient to fracture the ceramic ferrite or crack the NdFeB grain structure. Routine workflow repositioning between steel surfaces produces no measurable magnetization loss.

faq.question: What is the coating lifetime on the NdFeB SKUs?
faq.answer: The standard Ni-Cu-Ni triple-layer coating passes 500 h ASTM B117 salt-spray (ISO 2081 equivalent) and survives 5-10 years in standard indoor + mild-outdoor environments. The premium Ni-Cu-Ni + Parylene C CVD dual-coating passes 1000 h B117 + 500 h PCT (Pressure Cooker Test) and survives 10+ years in marine + washdown + chemical-plant environments. The N40 countersunk sanitary SKU uses 316L stainless welded-and-electropolished cover with effectively unlimited lifetime under CIP / SIP bioprocess wash-down.
